sources.entry: Agent Zero - A repository for creating and managing autonomous AI agents with customizable goals and tasks.

summary.one_liner: Agent Zero is an open, Docker-based agent framework that gives an AI agent its own Linux desktop, browser, document editors, plugins, and a bridge to the user's host machine.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Dockerized Linux environment where the agent can use an XFCE desktop in a Canvas panel, run terminals, and drive GUI apps such as Blender. A built-in browser supports page reading, clicking, typing, screenshots, and an Annotate mode where users click elements to inspect, change, or comment on them. Markdown, LibreOffice Writer/Calc/Impress (ODT/ODS/ODP) files can be co-edited with the agent. Projects isolate files, instructions, memory, secrets, and Git repos; Skills, Agent Profiles, and Model Presets change behavior; and agents can delegate work to subordinate agents. A Plugin Hub, MCP and A2A support, and a Time Travel snapshot/revert feature for the /a0/usr workspace extend it further. The A0 CLI Connector lets the agent work on files outside the container.
use_cases: run an autonomous agent on a full Linux desktop
annotate and re-implement web UI designs
co-edit documents and spreadsheets with an AI agent
isolate client or project memory and secrets
work in local git repositories from a Dockerized agent
delegate research or coding to subagents
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (A0 Install, macOS/Linux; URL not included in README text)
irm | iex  (A0 Install, Windows PowerShell; URL not included in README text)
curl -LsSf | sh  (A0 CLI Connector, macOS/Linux; URL not included in README text)
notable: Real XFCE Linux desktop inside the Canvas that the user can watch and take over
Browser Annotate mode to inspect, change, lift, or comment on page elements
Plugin Hub listing more than 100 community plugins
Time Travel snapshots, diffs, and revert for the /a0/usr workspace
A0 CLI Connector bridges a running instance to files on the host machine
caveats: Requires Docker; the README says it runs wherever Docker runs.
Granting host access (A0 CLI read/write and remote code execution) is powerful and should be limited to trusted machines and workspaces.
Time Travel is explicitly not a replacement for Git or backups.
